title: Your loudest month
text: September 2017 was the peak: 5,176 plays, about 62 hours of music.

title: The day you couldn't settle
text: On 6 September 2017 there were 1,816 plays in a single day, and 94% of them lasted under 30 seconds. That looks like searching, not listening.

title: The Beatles: the constant
text: The Beatles were the most-played artist in 8 of 10 full listening years (9% of all plays).

title: From devotion to discovery
text: In 2017 you played 647 different artists. In 2021 it was 1,578. Fewer plays, far more variety: the listener became an explorer.

title: How often you moved on
text: You hit the forward button on 52% of tracks in 2017, but only 18% in 2024.

title: Your listening clock
text: Listening peaks around 00:00 and is quietest around 12:00 (UTC+0).

title: From saving to spending
text: In 2016, 72% of the money spent or set aside went into saving and investing. By 2018 that fell to 59%, as everyday spending took a bigger share.

title: The two-wheeler
text: Between 3 Jan and 27 Jan 2018 3 payments totalling ₹94,000 bought a bike. After that came parking, a sticker, and the first servicing: a small arc of ownership.

title: The trip
text: 4 trip-related payments between 25 Jul and 28 Aug 2017 add up to ₹63,300, the largest travel spend in the records.

title: The steady paycheck
text: 43 salary credits from Feb 2015 to Aug 2018, about ₹58,758 each.

title: Small recurring things
text: 13 different subscriptions show up, from streaming to gas to online courses. 143 payments in total.

title: 2017: everything at once
text: 2017 is the peak year in two datasets at once: the most listening (26,320 plays) and the most everyday spending (₹442,575). Music and money rose together.

title: The card years
text: 1,276 distinct card transactions after removing 8,767 duplicate rows. Biggest category: travel (₹1,591,990). Busiest month: June 2023.

title: Half the card records are flagged
text: 54% of card transactions with a known status carry a fraud flag, far above any real-world rate. It is treated as a marker in this dataset, not a verdict.
